_comment: Baseline tick positions for `msuite upi --midi`. Same discipline as the
Serpe conformance vectors: what the notation SHOULD produce, pinned, so a
change that moves a note has to say so out loud.
All values are TICKS at 480 per quarter, 120 bpm — the renderer's defaults.
`onsets` are de-duplicated moments in time (simultaneous lanes count once);
`lanes` gives each note number's own timeline, which is how a poly file is
Never hand-edit a value to make a test pass. If the renderer changed on
purpose, regenerate and put WHY in the commit; if it changed by accident,
that is the bug this file exists to catch.

vectors.name: mono E(3,8)
vectors.why: The plainest case. Step = 120 ticks, onsets at steps 0,3,6, cycle = 960.

vectors.name: mono E(5,8) with accents
vectors.why: An accent is louder AND transposed +5, so accented onsets appear on note 41. Two note numbers here is the two-channel accent, visible in the file.

vectors.name: poly E(3,8)/E(3,7) — cycle lock (polyrhythm)
vectors.why: Both lanes span ONE cycle of 960 ticks, so lane 2's seven steps are 137.14 ticks each. Both lanes start cycle 2 at 960 — that shared 960 is what makes it polyrhythm.

vectors.name: poly E(3,8)/E(3,7) — step lock (polymeter)
vectors.why: Every lane's step is 120 ticks, so the 7-step lane finishes early: it starts cycle 2 at 840 while lane 1 starts at 960. That drift is the polymeter, and it is the single clearest difference between the two locks.

vectors.name: poly with per-lane accents
vectors.why: D8 — an accent layer belongs to its lane. Lane 1 accents onsets 1 and 3 (note 36+5=41); lane 2's {11} accents every onset (note 37+5=42). Four note numbers.

vectors.name: single lane, whole cycle
vectors.why: One onset per cycle. Guards the degenerate case where an off-by-one in cycle length would be invisible in a busier pattern.
